analysis: The code snippet defines a method `encodeHashToOIDC` that takes a byte array `hash`, computes half its length, copies it using `Arrays.copyOf`, and Base64Url-encodes the result. The `Arrays.copyOf` method can throw `NullPointerException` if the original array is null, and `NegativeArraySizeException` if the new length is negative. In this context, `hash` is the parameter; there is no null check, so if `hash` is null, a `NullPointerException` will be thrown. For non-null `hash`, `hash.length` is non-negative, so `hashLength` (hash.length / 2) is always non-negative, thus `NegativeArraySizeException` is avoided. Therefore, only `NullPointerException` is not avoided.
remark: The `NullPointerException` is triggered if the `hash` parameter passed to `encodeHashToOIDC` is null, because `Arrays.copyOf` will attempt to access the null reference. There is no null check in the code to prevent this. The `NegativeArraySizeException` is avoided because `hash.length` (for a non-null array) is always non-negative, so `hashLength` computed as `hash.length / 2` is also non-negative; thus the condition for this exception never occurs.
